articles.author: GridCircuits
articles.description:
An arc-flash study hands you a number: so many calories per square centimetre, at a stated working distance, for a stated arc duration. That number is useful, but it is also frozen in place. Change one thing about the fault, and the number may no longer apply.
The question this article answers is a narrow one: if nothing else changes, what happens to that incident-energy result when only the arc duration changes? That is exactly what the GridCircuits scaling calculator does, and it is worth understanding why the answer turns on clearing time — the speed of your protection.
The tool starts from a reference incident-energy result that must come from a validated incident-energy study. It does not perform a complete IEEE 1584 calculation, and it does not calculate arcing current, arc-flash bou…
articles.title: Arc-Flash Scaling: Why Clearing Time Is the Lever You Actually Control

Most of the surprises come from three places: payment methods that don't complete instantly, price points that were copied from another market, and purchase logic that assumes the player's app stays open until the payment finishes.
Here is the checklist we'd run through before a soft launch in India. It assumes Google Play Billing (directly or through Unity IAP or another wrapper), but most of it applies to any store.
Players in India often pay with UPI or other methods that can take time to confirm, and they may switch to their payments app to approve the transaction. Make sure your game handles the PENDING purchase state properly:
Don't …
articles.title: In-App Purchases for Players in India: A Google Play Billing Checklist Before Your Soft Launch

articles.author: Anuj Sadani
articles.description:
A reader spending ten minutes on an explanation might be learning carefully, struggling, or leaving the tab open. Reading time alone cannot tell you which.
If the goal is understanding, ask the reader to do something that requires it: trace a request, identify a failure boundary, or choose where a change belongs. Then retain the answer and explain how it was scored.
Comprehension Bench is a local tool for organizing that kind of small comparison. The shipped study is synthetic. It demonstrates the bookkeeping without claiming that one explanation actually teaches better than another.
The example compares two artifact conditions, ordinary documentation and an interactive explanation, using three tasks about a document preview flow. Participants have pseudonymous IDs and explicit assignments…

articles.author: Revercue
articles.description:
Last spring a client opened a proposal I had sent nine months earlier and replied: "happy to go ahead at this price." The price was from a different year, the scope named a framework version nobody used any more, and the site it referenced had been redesigned twice. Nothing about that reply was wrong. The document was simply still alive when it should have been finished.
A PDF has an accidental expiry: it gets lost, buried, or superseded. A link does not. A link is a promise that the document will be there, and if you never revoke that promise, you are running an archive you did not plan. This is the part of the tracked-link workflow nobody writes about, because it happens after the interesting design decisions: deciding how long a client document should live, and what everyone sees on the…
articles.title: Your proposal link should expire — plan for the day it does

articles.author: Cenk KURTOĞLU
articles.description:
Security checklists are easy to write and hard to act on. Below is the actual report produced by twelve read-only catalogue checks against a deliberately drifting local PostgreSQL 17 container. It is a synthetic fixture: no customer project, no hosted database, no production connection. The point is the shape of the output and the kind of state it catches.
The checks ran as a catalogue-only role created from a small SQL template: CONNECT on the database and USAGE on public, with no SELECT grant on any application table. All twelve checks completed. A direct SELECT * FROM public.orders under the same role returned permission denied for table orders.
That boundary is the design constraint. A nightly drift check should see security-relevant catalogue state without seeing customer rows. No ser…
articles.title: Nine findings from a real RLS drift check on PostgreSQL 17 (synthetic fixture)

articles.author: Anuj Sadani
articles.description:
A feature can sound settled until someone asks about a specific combination of inputs.
An editor can share a document. Inactive members cannot share. What happens when an editor's membership is inactive?
That question can surface in a planning meeting, during implementation, or after release. Intent Workbench provides a small place to examine such cases before the rules are embedded in application code.
The inputs are explicit facts such as role, visibility, and membership status. The model is a bounded decision table supplied by the team. The evaluator shows which rules match and whether they resolve to a consistent outcome.
The important distinction is between a model that can be parsed and a model whose rules cover a particular case. A structurally valid table can contain conflicting be…
articles.title: Run a Feature Decision Table Before Writing the Implementation

articles.author: Weeksafe
articles.description:
Weeksafe is a budgeting app for freelancers with irregular income. The promise is simple: one number for the week, after a tax reserve and the bills that are due soon. And we never ask for a bank login.
That last part is a product rule, not a slogan. It shaped how we take in transactions, how the homepage picks a currency, and how the free tax tools work. This post is about those three pieces.
A lot of finance apps start with "connect your bank." We did not want that as the way in. Open banking is a product of its own, and we would rather ship something honest that works in the UK, the US and elsewhere on day one.
So the main path is a bank-statement CSV. You download it from your bank's app or website, choose the file in Weeksafe, and we parse it on your device with PapaParse. The file is…
articles.title: How we import UK and US bank CSVs in the browser — and show £, $ or ₹ before the first paint

articles.description:
Two bigcommerce-api-mcp Body Matches and the Authentication Check They Cannot Answer


When an MCP package name appears in an HTTP body, the observation may point to a deployment guide, a status page, or a running transport endpoint. CVE-2026-138034 affected bigcommerce-api-mcp before 1.0.1 because the /sse and /messages routes skipped authentication. Internet search can help find candidates, but the decisive check is a request-level authentication test.
On 2026-11-27 at 23:43 UTC, ZoomEye was queried with http.body="bigcommerce-api-mcp" using sub_type=all, page 1, and page size 1. The successful query returned two matching assets.
A body match is not an application fingerprint. It confirms that the indexed response contained the package phrase. It does not establish that the server is run…
articles.title: Two bigcommerce-api-mcp Body Matches and the Authentication Check They Cannot Answer

articles.description:
The Problem With Cloud AI


Every token costs money. Every API call adds up. And your data goes to their servers.
brew install ollama
ollama pull llama3.2
ollama serve

Now you have a GPT-4 level model running on your MacBook. Free. Private. Fast.

def ask_local_ai(question):

    return r.json()["response"]
